section.title: Logs, Trash, downloads and personal data
section.intro: Logs, the Trash, installers, and data that belongs to you.

rules.title: Trash
rules.whatItIs: Items you already moved to the Trash.
rules.consequence: They would be deleted for good.
rules.sideCondition: Use Empty Trash in Finder. The Trash frees nothing until it is emptied.

rules.title: Logs
rules.whatItIs: Records apps and the system wrote about what they did.
rules.consequence: You would lose logs that help diagnose a past crash.
rules.sideCondition: Skip files changed in the last hour.

rules.title: Logs macOS writes
rules.whatItIs: Logs and crash reports that macOS writes for you.
rules.consequence: macOS manages these, so they are not offered for removal.

rules.title: Downloaded installers
rules.consequence: If this is your only copy, such as licensed software or an old version, it is gone for good.
rules.sideCondition: Move to Trash only. Whether the app is already installed is a guess.

rules.title: Mail attachment copies
rules.whatItIs: Copies of attachments you opened from Mail.
rules.consequence: Only the copies go; the originals stay in the messages.

rules.title: Mail data
rules.consequence: Manual deletion can corrupt Mail, and some messages may exist nowhere else.

rules.title: Messages data
rules.consequence: Manual deletion can corrupt your history, and it may be the only copy.

rules.title: Photos library
rules.whatItIs: Your photo library and its service data.
rules.consequence: Changes inside it can corrupt the library, and the originals may be the only copies.
rules.sideCondition: Free space from within Photos instead.

rules.title: Embedded browser cache
rules.whatItIs: A cache kept by an app that embeds a web browser.
rules.consequence: It rebuilds on its own, though some web apps keep offline-only data in the service worker cache.
rules.sideCondition: Close the app first. IndexedDB, Local Storage and Cookies are not caches.
